pr_title: Fix canvas state getting out of sync from smasks. (bug 1755507)
pr_body:
Soft masks can be enabled/disabled at anytime and at different
points in the save/restore stack. This can lead to
the amount of save/restores becoming unbalanced across the
two canvases. Instead of save/restoring on the temporary canvas
change it so we only track state on the main (suspended canvas).

I was also getting an out balance stack from patterns, so I've also
fixed that and added a warning that will at least show up on chrome.
It would be nice to add this so Firefox at some point too.

Fixes https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/11328, https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/14297 and bug 1755507

issue_context.title: Images embedded in PDF disappearing
issue_context.body:
I am using this test link [https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html)

The test pdf [pdfjs_lost_image_test.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/3840182/pdfjs_lost_image_test.pdf)

![pdfjs_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17464719/68747444-84d7f400-0635-11ea-8b36-d4902b4a359b.png)

The image is lost when previewing with pdfjs.

![pdfjs_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17464719/68747462-8d302f00-0635-11ea-8d76-347e00081066.png)

A temporary solution is to convert the file itself, convert this pdf to jpg first, and then convert this jpg to pdf.

Is it possible that the font is Chinese traditional? and how can I solve it?

Thanks a million!
comments: I don't see the images either using Firefox 70.0.1 (64-bit, Linux). The strange thing is that there are also no warnings/errors in the console, which I would have expected. Thank you for reporting this.
I have some question.....could somebody help this?

There is a regression in `SVG` rendering of the page in `2.10.377` ❌.

```
Error: Unknown IR type: p
    at i._makeShadingPattern
    at i.shadingFill
    at i.executeOpTree
    at i.group
    at i.executeOpTree
```

---

(latest known working version `2.8.335` ✔️ without any rendering issues).

> There is a regression in `SVG` rendering of the page

Please note that as mentioned in the Wiki, see https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions#backends, the SVG-backend is *not officially supported*.
Furthermore, this issue is about the default (i.e. `canvas`) backend specifically; hence let's avoid confusing things by not trying to track multiple things here :-)

> *not officially supported*

means do not bother us with reports, we are privately messing with it? I am good with that :-)

I just truly love that backend and wish all the best for it!

This is now getting really off-topic, but as explained previously the SVG-backend doesn't perform well enough for most real world applications (since it leads to *huge* number of DOM elements which browsers don't handle well); hence why development stopped.
This was *mostly* fixed by PR #14175 (only the cloud with the "Ethernet" text looks wrong now).

review_comments: Can't you simply reset the transform stack *unconditionally* here, since then I believe that you could remove line 212 below?
I don't think so, because then we'd end up attaching a _transformStack on canvases in Firefox which don't use this code.

In that case, shouldn't this new block of code simply be removed?
Note that the transform stack is already being [forcibly reset further down](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/d9a3a243533de06a61b94765178c3e4d826c8a43/src/display/canvas.js#L208), in non-Firefox browsers, which ought to render this new code block unnecessary.

In non-firefox browser the first time this code runs it will add a `ctx.mozCurrentTransform` to the context, so each subsequent call this function will return early. Since it returns early, the `_transformStack` won't forcibly reset without this new code.
